## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 26 (*Pallatthika*, "Clasping the knees") is a training rule from the *Sekhiya* section of the Vinaya Piṭaka's Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga. The rule addresses bodily decorum for monastic conduct in inhabited areas, specifically prohibiting sitting with one's knees clasped or "lolling" by supporting oneself with the hands or with strips of cloth wrapped around the legs and body [Horner]. An English translation of the rule and its associated case narrative is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
